KDA (local) or MLA + Inkling (global)"}} MIX --> SCA["ShortConv (MLA layers only)"] --> PA(["partial = attn out"]) PA --> GM["AttnRes gate
history + partial"] Hin --> GM GM --> M1["RMSNorm → GatedNorm"] --> MOE{{"LatentMoE + 2 shared experts"}} MOE --> SCM["ShortConv"] --> PB(["block b_i = attn out + MoE out"]) PB --> Hout[("appended to history")] ``` **3a. Kimi Delta Attention, the local mixer (layers 0, 1, 2, 4 at d512; D = 512, 4 heads × 128).** ```mermaid flowchart TB kx["x"] --> kq["q = SiLU(ShortConv(x W_q))"] & kk["k = SiLU(ShortConv(x W_k))"] & kv["v = SiLU(ShortConv(x W_v))"] kx --> kg["decay g = −5 · σ(exp(A_log) · (x W_a↓ W_a↑ + dt_bias))
rank-128 gate, per channel; A_log per head"] kx --> kb["write strength β = σ(x W_β), per head"] kq & kk --> kn["L2-norm q, k; q × 1/√128"] kn & kv & kg & kb --> rec["delta rule, chunked Pallas kernels (chunk 16)
S_t = (I − β k kᵀ) Diag(e^g) S_{t−1} + β k vᵀ
o_t = S_tᵀ q_t · state resets at document starts"] rec --> kon["per-head RMSNorm (shared 128-wide scale)"] --> kog["× σ(x W_g), per channel"] --> ko["W_o → sublayer out
no RoPE, no window, no output ShortConv"] ``` **3b. MLA + Inkling, the global mixer (layers 3 and 5 at d512).** ```mermaid flowchart TB mx["x"] --> mq["q = x W_q (full rank, 4 × 128)"] mx --> ml["KV latent = RMSNorm(x W_dkv), 512 wide, learnable gain"] --> mk["k = latent W_uk"] & mv["v = latent W_uv"] mx --> rel["Inkling bias[h,i,j] = R[i,h,:] · P[:, i−j]
R = x W_r (16 per head) · P 16 × 1024, shared across heads"] mq & mk & mv & rel --> fa["FA4 causal attention (fwd + SM90 bwd)
logits × 1/√128 (qk_mult 1) · no RoPE · no QK-norm
Inkling bias added before softmax"] fa --> xsa["XSA: subtract each head's component along its own v"] --> mg["× 2σ(x W_gate), per head, zero-init"] --> mo["W_o → ShortConv → sublayer out"] ``` **3c. LatentMoE with quantile-balanced routing (every layer).** ```mermaid flowchart TB ex["x (512)"] --> fused["one fused GEMM:
router · W_latent↓ · shared-expert gate/up"] fused --> rt["router logits (fp32)
top-(8+1) on logit − β_QB; 9th = threshold α"] rt --> qb["QB: β_e = global (1 − 8/384) quantile of logit − α
10k-bin histogram each step; router bias = −β, not trained"] rt --> cw["combine weights = σ(unbiased logits) of the top 8,
renormalized to sum to 2.5"] fused --> lat["latent = RMSNorm(x W_latent↓), 256 wide"] lat & cw --> ep["384 SwiGLU experts, hidden 256
pooled-wave EP all-to-all over 8 GPUs, capacity 1.15"] ep --> up["W_latent↑ 256 → 512"] fused --> sh["2 shared SwiGLU experts, 512 → 256 → 512
down projections fused into one GEMM"] up & sh --> sum["routed + shared → ShortConv → sublayer out"] ``` ¹ AttnRes rolls a new block at layer *i* while `i % max(1, L // 8) == 0` and fewer than 8 blocks exist. At d512 and d768 every layer closes a block. At d1024 (12 layers) and d1280 (14 layers) only layers 0–7 do, so layers 8 and up all accumulate into one running partial instead of their own blocks. **Optimizer routing:** - **MuonH:** every attention and MoE matrix, and every GatedNorm (KDA `W_β` at 2× the MuonH LR). - **AdamH:** lm_head. - **Adam:** embedding, router, attention output gate, norm gains, ShortConv kernels, KDA decay parameters, Inkling weights. - **Adam at 0.1× the Adam LR:** the AttnRes queries. ## Baseline: clean KMA Branch [`fasttrack-moe-kma`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/fasttrack-moe-kma) @ `4eba59cafa`. Build from this branch. The recipe below covers every model and optimizer component. Values are for d512 unless noted; the code is `experiments/grug/fast_track/{model,optimizer,heuristic,launch}.py`. **Shape** | Rung | Width D | Layers | Local (KDA) / global (MLA) layers | Heads × head dim | Batch | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | d512 | 512 | 6 | 4 / 2 | 4 × 128 | 128 | | d768 | 768 | 8 | 6 / 2 | 6 × 128 | 128 | | d1024 | 1024 | 12 | 9 / 3 | 8 × 128 | 256 | | d1280 | 1280 | 14 | 10 / 4 | 10 × 128 | 256 | - Every 4th layer and the last layer are global; all other layers are local. - The run uses a 16k vocab and sequence length 4096 with packed documents. Every ShortConv and the KDA state respect document boundaries (the KDA state resets at each document start). - Weights are initialized with std 0.5/√D. Compute is bf16. **Embedding and output** - Token embedding → RMSNorm → GatedNorm. The result is AttnRes source 0. - Output path: final AttnRes gate → RMSNorm → GatedNorm → untied lm_head (`output_proj`). - The fused lm_head + cross-entropy loop uses a vocab tile of 8192. - GatedNorm (every GatedNorm in the model) is `x · sigmoid(W_up · SiLU(W_down · x))`, with a rank-128 bottleneck. **Block (every layer)** - **Attention sublayer:** input = its AttnRes gate mix → RMSNorm → GatedNorm → mixer (KDA or MLA). - **MoE sublayer:** input = its AttnRes gate mix → RMSNorm → GatedNorm → MoE → ShortConv on the MoE output. - Each ShortConv is a 4-tap causal depthwise conv. **Local layers: Kimi Delta Attention** (Kimi K3's layer) - **Projections:** q/k/v are D → N·128 with full heads (no GQA). Each goes through a ShortConv followed by SiLU. q and k are L2-normalized, and q is scaled by 1/√128. - **Decay:** per-channel log-decay `g = −5·sigmoid(exp(A_log)·(x·W_a_down·W_a_up + dt_bias))`. - The gate projection has rank 128. - `A_log` is one value per head, initialized to 0. - `dt_bias` is one value per channel, initialized so the decay rate spans 0.02–0.5. - **Write strength:** `β = sigmoid(x·W_β)`, one value per head. - **Recurrence:** `S_t = (I − β·k·kᵀ)·Diag(exp(g))·S_{t−1} + β·k·vᵀ`, read out as `o_t = S_tᵀ·q_t`. - It runs as chunked Pallas kernels, with a stable block-doubling inverse inside each chunk. - **Output:** per-head RMSNorm with a learnable 128-wide scale shared across heads → full-rank per-channel gate `sigmoid(x·W_g)` → `W_o`. - No positional encoding, no window, no XSA, and no ShortConv on the branch output. **Global layers: MLA + Inkling relative position** - **q:** full-rank, D → N·128 (no Q latent). - **k and v:** k = `W_uk · RMSNorm(x·W_dkv)` and v = `W_uv · RMSNorm(x·W_dkv)`. - They share one 512-wide KV latent, with a learnable RMSNorm on the latent. - Heads are 128 wide with no RoPE part. - There's no ShortConv on K, so the up-projections can be absorbed at inference. - **Scaling:** no QK-norm; `qk_mult` = 1, i.e. standard 1/√128 logit scaling. - **Position — Inkling relative-position bias**, added to the pre-softmax logits in place of RoPE: - `bias[h,i,j] = R[i,h,:] · P[:, i−j]`, where `R = x·W_r` is 16 values per head. - `P` is a bank of shape [16 × 1024] shared across heads. The relative extent is 1024. - It runs inside the FA4 attention kernel (forward, backward, and the SM90 backward pass). - **XSA** (exclusive self-attention): subtract the component of each head's output that is parallel to its own value vector. - **Output gate:** per head, `2·sigmoid(x·W_gate)`. `W_gate` is zero-initialized, so the gate is 1 at init. - The branch output also gets a ShortConv. **MoE sublayer (LatentMoE with quantile-balanced routing)** - **Experts:** 384 routed experts, top-8. Each is a SwiGLU with hidden size D/2. - **Latent space:** experts operate in a D/2-wide latent. The input goes through `W_latent_down` → RMSNorm, and the combined expert output goes back up through `W_latent_up`. - **Router:** reads the full-width token and computes logits in fp32. - Experts are selected by top-(8+1) on bias-adjusted logits, where the 9th logit is the threshold α. - Combine weights are the sigmoid of the unbiased logits, renormalized to sum to 2.5. - **Quantile balancing:** each step, each expert's threshold β is the global (1 − K/E) quantile of the logit margins (logit − α), read from a 10k-bin histogram. The router bias is set to −β. - The router bias is not trained by gradient. - **Capacity:** capacity factor 1.15, with pooled-wave expert-parallel dispatch. Receiver ranks are sort-based and the expand backward is gather-based. - **Shared experts:** 2 shared SwiGLU experts that bypass the latent: D → D/2 hidden → D. - **Fused projections:** - The router, latent-down, and both shared experts' gate/up projections run as one GEMM. - The shared experts' down-projections run as one GEMM. **Residual stream: Block Attention Residuals** - **Sources:** the embedding source, one running sum per completed block of sublayer outputs, and the running partial sum of the current block. - The model has 8 blocks. Block sums use the raw sublayer outputs. - **Gates:** every sublayer (attention and MoE) has its own gate, and there is one final gate before the output norm. Each gate has one learned pseudo-query `q ∈ ℝᴰ`, zero-initialized so every gate starts as a uniform average. - **Mixing:** per token, `logitᵢ = q · rms_norm(sourceᵢ)`, using a parameter-free (frozen) RMS key norm, then `softmax` over sources and a weighted sum of the raw sources. - **Implementation:** - Each completed block is scored once against every gate that reads it. - Backward: at d512 the layer's forward intermediates are saved. At d768–d1280 each layer is recomputed. At d1280 the attention branch is also rematerialized. - The model keeps one layer stack per mixer kind. **Optimizer** | Group | Update rule | LR | Parameters | |---|---|---|---| | `muonh` | MuonH | MuonH LR | all attention and MoE matrices: MLA `W_q`/`W_dkv`/`W_uk`/`W_uv`/`W_o`; KDA `W_q`/`W_k`/`W_v`/`W_o`/`W_g`; experts; shared experts; latent down/up. Also every GatedNorm `W_down`/`W_up`. | | `kda_beta` | MuonH | 2 × MuonH LR | KDA `W_β` | | `adamh` | AdamH | MuonH LR | lm_head (`output_proj`) | | `adam` | Adam | Adam LR | token embedding; router; attention output gate; router bias slot (overwritten by QB); all 1-D norm gains; ShortConv kernels; KDA `W_a_down`/`W_a_up`, `A_log`, `dt_bias`; Inkling `W_r` and `P` | | `attn_res_query` | Adam | 0.1 × Adam LR | the AttnRes pseudo-queries | - **MuonH:** Nesterov momentum 0.95 → Newton–Schulz orthogonalization (5 quintic steps, bucketed across same-shape matrices) → a step along that direction, then projection back onto the matrix's Frobenius sphere. Each matrix's norm stays fixed at its init value. - **AdamH:** the Adam direction with the same Frobenius-sphere (hyperball) projection. - **Adam:** β1 0.9. Only the router and the attention output gate get decoupled weight decay (0.02). No other parameter gets weight decay, and there's no gradient clipping. - **Schedule:** 1% warmup, then linear decay to 0.05× peak. - **Peak values** from `MoeHeuristic` (they depend on tokens, width and batch): - Adam LR = `0.0876 · tokens^−0.346 · D^−0.345 · √(tokens per batch)`. - MuonH LR = 13/3 × Adam LR. - β2 = `0.999^(tokens per batch / 131072)`. - ε = `9.68e−18 · √(steps)`. - At d512 with 2384 steps: MuonH LR 0.0227, Adam LR 0.0052, β2 0.996, ε 4.7e−16. Submit (the default priority is interactive): ``` NO_PROXY="*" uv run python -m experiments.grug.fast_track.launch --submit \ --target-cluster cw-us-east-02a --priority interactive \ --run-id --size d512 --recipe kma --num-steps <8-min steps> --version ``` ## Compute - cw-us-east-02a at **interactive** priority. - **At most 10 active runs at once**, probes included. - **Limit runs above d768** to keep the experimentation rate high. d1024 and d1280 runs take hours and hold a slot the whole time, so save them for changes that have already passed gate 1 or that need extra scales because of curve-fitting risk. - Don't save checkpoints (the launcher default). ## For humans Comment with a research direction for the agent, for example "try X", or "combine A and B". The agent picks up new comments at its next batch. The main goal of a single experiment should be to learn about the system. This means that if you tweak one knob and the loss goes off the rails, the experiment can still be considered a success! We better understand the system sensitivity! Building knowledge through failed experiments will bring us closer to the long term goal of better models. ## For the agent - Read `experiments/grug/fast_track/README.md` and `agent.md` first. Where they differ from this issue, this issue wins; the main difference is the fixed-time objective. - Run 5–10 experiments per batch, and prioritize human comments when picking the next one. - Ask for clarification in the thread if helpful, but never hold a batch waiting for an answer: state your assumption and correct it in the next batch. - Start at d512. When a change beats the current best by more than 0.005, validate it at d768. - Post **one comment per batch** and edit it as runs finish. Start it with 🤖 and include: - the batch goal, and which human comments it addresses; - a table with one row per run: change | branch@commit | W&B link | steps | ex/s | mid loss | final Paloma macro loss | Δ vs current best; - a 1–3 line takeaway and the planned next batch. - **Branches:** prefix with `ladderclimb_v1_`, and link the exact commit each job ran. - **W&B:** project `marin_moe`, with short prefixed run IDs such as `lc1-b03-…` (names over 128 characters fail at init). - Add the `agent-generated` label to any issue or PR you open. - Keep the **Status** table below updated with a concise chronology of improvements. ## Studies Deep dives and multi-batch studies, newest first. Pages are claude.ai artifacts; batch comments hold the plan, every run and the numbers. | study | what it found | page | batch comments | |---|---|---|---| | **Hyperball decay per matrix** | The MuonH/AdamH hyperball re-projection acts as a per-matrix weight decay that depends on the update's direction (`decay = 1 − |W|/|W+u|` ≈ `lr·cos(W,u) + lr²/2`). Logged every step for every matrix on the ragged base (`lc1-b191-hb2`, 2.9631). Typical matrices decay 0.06–0.10%/step mid-run with cos ≈ 0.07–0.10, so over 90% of the decay comes from updates leaning outward, not from the orthogonal part. Odd ones: KDA `w_beta` (all 4 layers) decays 2–3× anything else (0.17–0.26%/step, 1.3% early) with 4× the rescale and inward swings; the AdamH lm head has the lowest median (0.045%) but the largest spikes (p99 1.27%, cos up to 0.66); layer-5 MLA `w_o` spikes too (p99 1.0%); layer-5 MLA `w_uv` is the only large projection with inward steps; gated-norm matrices hold the highest sustained decay, rising with depth. Code: `--opt-set log_hyperball_decay=true` (`hyperball_metrics`). | [Hyperball Decay Atlas](https://claude.ai/artifact/74PcjNW2PaNkYV5btbq3Ug) | — | | **Learned RMSNorm gains** | What every learned RMSNorm gain learns on candidate 11 (linear gains), per module. No gain goes negative; gains span about 700× across modules (`embed2_norm` 0.01–0.45, `final_norm` up to 7.6) but cluster tightly within one, and the largest (`final_norm`, MoE latent norms) are still rising at the end. Gain functions: `e^w` −0.0026 (within noise; `final_norm` climbs to 15), softplus −0.0008, `2·sigmoid` +0.115 (pins `final_norm` at its cap of 2). Learned output scalars on every sublayer are neutral (linear −0.0003, `2·sigmoid` −0.0015). The seen batch keeps improving after the update: −0.49 nats/token peak 15 steps later at step 1000, −0.24 peak about 50 steps later at step 2200 (momentum; the slow AdEMAMix buffer has about a 50-step memory). The early gain is mostly forgotten by step 2200 (≈ −0.01); the late one mostly stays (−0.19 at the end, EMA too). The conversion rule predicted about −0.007. Each candidate's own 480 s step count comes from 300-step `--no-eval` timing probes. This is the first time both ran at exactly 480 s; the 2817-step numbers were 490–525 s of training. The tail-stack layers' extra ~10 ms per step is what keeps the fixed-time gain small. - **Retention:** about 79% log-k from d512 to d768. - **Runtime, from 2026-10-01** ([notes](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9451#issuecomment-5934720837)): - **Train step:** jitted over the state's flat leaves, which cuts host dispatch (−6.9% step at the same math). - **PGLE:** off for ML runs. It caused most of the `CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_FAILED` restarts; turning it off costs about +3% step time at the same loss. - **Evals:** one final eval on the pure EMA weights. The midpoint eval and the EMA-blend sweep are gone. ### Candidate 9 (previous best) **Runtime (adopted 2026-09-30, no ML change):** PGLE (`--pgle-runs 5`) and the XLA autotune cache syncing every 30 min ([`b25ed70f4a`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/b25ed70f4a)). At d768 (widths scaled to hidden, 7325 steps): **2.7153 / 2.7098**, −0.0051 vs candidate 8 with **107% log-k retention**. The rules, following the MFU-gaming guidance: - changes are judged at equal steps; - 8 active experts stay, and the MoE latent stays at 0.5d; - expert/shared widths scale with hidden_dim; - the recipe must fit d1024 on 8×H100 (candidate 8 does, with attention remat). lm_head z-loss kept - MLA partial key offset (`mla_key_offset=true`) - per-head key RMSNorm on the MLA layers (`mla_k_norm=true`) - per-head query RMSNorm on the MLA layers (`mla_q_norm=true`); free under MLA absorption, since queries aren't cached *KDA:* - Gated DeltaNet-2 channel-wise erase and write gates (`kda_erase_gate=true`, `kda_write_gate=true`) *Embeddings and memory:* - gated value embeddings on the MLA layers (`value_embeds=gated`) - no GatedNorm on the embedding or the lm_head input (`embed_gated_norm=false`, `final_gated_norm=false`) - 524k-row hashed bigram table as an AttnRes source, table LR ×10 (`second_embed=true`, `second_embed_bigram=true`, `embed2_rows=524288`, `embed2_lr_mult=10`) - rank-16 per-channel content gate on the bigram source (`bigram_gate=true`, `bigram_gate_rank=16`) *Experts:* - 512 routed experts, top-8, i.e. sparsity 64 (`num_experts=512`) - one shared expert of width 1.5d instead of two of 0.75d (`num_shared_experts=1`, `shared_expert_intermediate_dim=768`) - ungated ReLU² experts at 1.5× width, routed and shared (`moe_ungated_relu2=true`, `moe_ungated_kernel=true`, `shared_ungated_relu2=true`, `intermediate_dim=384`, `shared_expert_intermediate_dim=384`) *Router and MoE combine (candidate 9):* - router Adam LR ×0.5 (`router_lr_mult=0.5`) - sqrt-softplus combine weights (`router_combine=sqrt_softplus_renorm`) - drop-aware combine renorm: renormalize the surviving slots when an assignment is dropped at capacity (`moe_drop_renorm=true`) - MuonH sigmoid-gate init ×2 (`init_std_mult_gates=2`) *Optimizer:* - Adam β1 0.8 (`beta1=0.8`) - MuonEq per-input normalization (`muon_pre_norm=in`) - Bi-Maxwell momentum on MuonH (`muon_bimaxwell=true`) - MuonH LR decay `1 − p^0.7` (`muonh_decay_power=0.7`); topics.title: Support context-length switches in the hero run
topics.body:
Let the hero switch context length mid-run without changing its training schedule. The ladder launcher takes `--seq-len` and holds 4,194,304 tokens per rack per update, so the sequence batch shrinks as the context grows (2816 sequences at 16K on 11 racks). The step count (390251), learning rates, decay, gate/router weight decay, and `run_progress` therefore match the 4K run. A changed context requires an explicit `--qk-mult`, applied to all attention layers; `--capacity-factor` overrides the expert receiver capacity.

Harrier now shuffles blocks of 2^20 tokens (`io_block_size = 2**20 // seq_len`), which equals the existing 256-sequence block at 4K. At a longer context the outer block permutation stays the same, so only each cell's in-progress 512-block window reorders. With the previous sequence-sized blocks, a 16K relaunch would have re-read an estimated 2.85T already-seen tokens of the remaining ~9T. At 16K the past main-mixture boundary moves from step 108000 to 108096, and a continuation must pass `--accept-mixture-boundary-shift`.

Canonical hero eval stays at 4K packing, so the inherited `eval_dropless/*` series remains comparable, and the first-step eval now also runs after a checkpoint resume. Per-example FLOPs rise with context, so a FLOPs baseline (`--flops-baseline-step`, `--flops-baseline-total`) keeps `throughput/total_gflops` continuous across the handoff. `trigger_hero.sh` records the context, QK multiplier, capacity, eval context, FLOPs baseline, and boundary acceptance in the W&B lineage and the #8506 launch record. `launch_diagnostics` gains `--optimizer-tokens-per-step`, `--gate-router-weight-decay`, `--eval-seq-len`, and `--eval-prefix`, so a one-rack rehearsal can use the hero's optimizer settings and report long-context eval separately.

The live run is unchanged. A switch still needs a GPU rehearsal from the handoff checkpoint and agreed trial thresholds; see the inventory and validation plan in #9615.

Part of #9615

topics.title: [grug] Select the hero router's top-k experts with a Triton kernel
topics.body:
The hero router's top-(K+1) expert selection runs in a Triton kernel instead of a full XLA sort of every row: 0.096 ms per call instead of 0.856 ms at [65536, 384], k = 9 on one GB200, once in the forward and again in the recompute. The indices and their order match `jax.lax.top_k` bitwise for every input, including ties, signed zeros, infinities and NaNs.

XLA:GPU uses its own top-k kernel only for rows of at least 1,024 elements, so 384-expert rows fall back to a sort. The new kernel takes float32 rows narrower than 1,024 on a GPU device; everything else keeps `jax.lax.top_k`. Its gate asks the default device whether it is a GPU (`levanter.grug._moe.availability`), because a hero test stubs `jax.default_backend` to trace a GPU-only path on CPU devices. The Triton gather-sum's gate moves to the same check.

One warp holds one row in registers, as one power-of-two tile or, when that pads less, three equal ones (a 384-wide row is three 128-wide tiles), and takes k successive maxima over XLA's float32 total-order key, breaking ties by the lower column. A row in one warp keeps both reductions inside the warp; Triton reduces across warps through shared memory. A taken or absent entry gets the smallest key and the column n, which the lowest-column reduction never returns, so a negative NaN with payload 0xFFFFFFFF, whose key is also the smallest, is not mistaken for one. The kernel reads an int32 view of the input, so autodiff never asks it for a JVP rule. For k above 16 the steps run in a loop, which compiles in 0.2 s where unrolled steps take 36 s at k = 384.

No rack run measured this kernel alone. On one 64-GPU hero rack (restore step-180000, seed 0, 100 steps), an earlier version that took 0.125 ms per call shortened the step by 0.53%.

Split from #9708. Part of #9636.

belayNew.body:
🤖 **Partial key offset study: what the shifted half of the MLA heads learns** (d512 current best / candidate 12, EMA weights of `lc1-b234-attn-distance`, 2.9528)

With `mla_key_offset`, each MLA head's first 64 key channels come from the previous token (j−1); channels 64–127 come from the current token. I looked at what that split learns: the query/key directions of each head, then a probe of where the heads attend.

**Method**
- **Directions in the attention input x:** the query direction is the `W_q` column. The key direction is backed out through the latent: `W_dkv · diag(latent norm gain) · W_uk`, with the latent RMSNorm linearized.
- **The 128 per-channel pairs aren't unique:** any rotation of a head's channels gives the same scores. So each head is also analyzed through the SVD of its query–key product `B = W_q W_kᵀ`, which gives canonical (query direction, key direction, strength) pairs. The raw-channel and canonical numbers agree closely.

**1. The shifted half is an induction lookup, built into the weights**

Mean query/key cosine on the shifted half (channels 0–63), per head:

| head | layer 3 | layer 5 |
|---|---|---|
| H0 | 0.61 | 0.90 |
| H1 | 0.87 | 0.70 |
| H2 | 0.41 | 0.85 |
| H3 | 0.80 | 0.85 |
| H4 | 0.85 | 0.45 |
| H5 | 0.89 | 0.88 |

- **Query and key point the same way in all 12 heads.** By pair strength, 92–100% sits on positively matched pairs, and no head has negatively matched pairs. So a query scores keys whose *previous* token resembles its own token: "find where I appeared before and read what came next."
- **The current-token half matches only weakly** (+0.14 to +0.40), except L3 H2 (+0.87), a copy head.
- **The attention probe agrees.** Queries at fixed in-document positions (x = 20…4,000), with each query's full softmax row kept rather than averaged:
  - at x = 4,000, 30–49% of the top long-range keys of the sharp layer-3 heads (H1, H4, H5) are induction targets;
  - half of those heads' long-range mass sits on 6–36 keys;
  - L3 H2 picks earlier copies of the query token (33% of its top keys).
- **Layer-5 heads are induction-shaped in the weights too (0.85–0.93), but diffuse in behavior.** Half their long-range mass needs 93–172 keys. They likely match on broader features, so many keys qualify.

**2. The 64 shifted dims are not redundant in weight space**

| per head, shifted half | range |
|---|---|
| directions for 50% / 90% of B's strength | 11–19 / 40–48 |
| effective rank (of 64) | 41–55 |
| stable rank | 12–28 |
| average \|cos\| between different key channels | 0.04–0.07 |
| top 8 channels' share of strength (uniform = 0.125) | 0.14–0.15 |

The channels are near-orthogonal and none dominates. A dozen or so stronger directions plus a long real tail. This is weight space only: whether the data uses all 64 needs an activation-side rank or an ablation, which isn't run yet.

**3. Tying the query to the key on the shifted half costs nothing**

`mla_tie_prev_qk` (`b759695d8f`): the query's shifted half *is* the token's own un-shifted key half, so those channels score `k_prev(x_i) · k_prev(x_{j−1})`, a symmetric similarity. It needs no query projection for those 64 channels.

| run | Paloma | step ms |
|---|---|---|
| current best (`lc1-b217-ctrl`) | 2.9521 | 190.2 |
| **tied shifted half (`lc1-b236-tie-prev-qk`)** | **2.9517** | 190.3 |

Neutral: the free query directions were re-learning the key. That makes it a free simplification, and it drops 64 query columns per head in both MLA layers.

**4. For sparse attention**

The shifted half is close to a symmetric positive form, a learned similarity between the query token and each key's previous token. A low-rank index over previous-token states (around 16–32 dims) could pre-select long-range candidates for the retrieval heads. The diffuse layer-5 heads look better suited to pooled chunk summaries than to top-k selection.

**Next:**
- an activation-side effective rank of the shifted half;
- shifting 16 or 32 channels instead of 64;
- the Inkling relative-position bias by distance. That probe run (`lc1-b235-relpos-probe`) just finished.
